sections.html: Garra qiaojiensis occurs only very locally in the Irrawaddy system of China and Burma. The fish described here come from the Putao region in Burma.

The two specimens are approximately 9 cm long. One specimen has a red spot on its shoulder, which the other does not; there are also differences in the coloration of the pelvic fins, and one fish appears to be slimmer than the other. Based on these characteristics, they are believed to be a pair.

Many good aquarium fish have come from the extremely species-rich genus Garra, such as the doctor fish Garra rufa, Garra flavatra and Garra panitvongi. Garra qiaojiensis was received as two sample specimens with striking beauty. Only a small number of animals were available from the supplier.
